calibration.reference_10: Seeing Theory, Brown University (https://seeing-theory.brown.edu/), correlation/regression chapter — the learner drags points and watches r and the line of best fit recompute live under the hand.
calibration.reference_8: BBC Bitesize GCSE Maths, 'Representing data' / scatter-graph units (https://www.bbc.co.uk/bitesize) — the ladder's own 8 reference: assignable to a class unedited, correct and complete, if not memorable.

verdict: Every number in the three datasets matches the copy (72.5/71.4/1.8, 25.2%/57.4%/7.30 h, r = 0.81 collapsing to 0.26/0.10/0.31), all three activities now gate on a real experiment, feedback names the specific misconception, nuance is taught explicitly, and free text is handled honestly with a checklist and exemplar instead of fake grading. It stops short of the 8 bar because two activity-1 sentences are false against the screen itself: the hint says everything in the statistics box is a property of the data while the box's own 'gap as drawn' tile is a picture property, and the 'too relaxed' feedback hard-codes a 25x zoom that only holds for the 70-74 preset (60-80 gives 5x). Both fixes are paste-ready below; with them and the small activity-2 chart clamp this is assignable unedited.

blocking.fix: Compare the statistics box above with the chart. The first three tiles are properties of the data — they stay identical whatever the axis. The fourth tile, “gap as drawn”, is deliberately different: it is a property of the picture, because it measures the same 1.8-point gap against whatever axis you have chosen. Ask that question of anything else that moves when you drag a slider.

blocking.why_it_caps_score: A learner-facing number that can contradict what the learner actually saw — the defect class R1-ED-1 was raised for — inside the feedback that corrects the 'axis never matters' misconception.

non_blocking.issue: The a2 chart clamps every dot into the fixed 6.0-8.0 h window, so a draw outside it is plotted at the edge while the table and aria description show the true value (5 of the first 400 seeded random n=10 draws exceed 8.0 h, max 8.25 h; convenience n=10 can reach 8.07 h).

Educator guide sampling figures are looser than the seeded model: 'roughly 55-68% late-library users' (400 seeded draws: 10-90% at n=10, mean 56.3%; 40-76% at n=50; 53-63% at n=500) and 'about 0.4-0.65 h low' (the mean deficit is ~0.4 h at every size).
non_blocking.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The table makes the mechanism visible: convenience draws average about 57% late-library users against a true 25% (the sampler design gives 57.4%; at n=10 they range from about 10% to 90%, settling to 53-63% by n=500), and their mean sleep sits about 0.4 h low **regardless of size**, while random draws wobble at n=10 and converge by n=500."

keep: The 'gap as drawn (share of the axis height)' tile: the same 1.8-point gap reported as 1.8% at 0-100 and 45% at 70-74 turns 'the picture changed' into a number the learner can watch move while every data statistic stays frozen (app.js:160, model.js:30).

The experiment gates: a1 refuses to mark until two axis ranges have been tried, a2 until one draw of each method exists, a3 until the within-season toggle has been used plus a >=15-character justification (app.js:179, 268, 326-327).

The sampling model: one 1,200-student population shown beside every draw, deterministic seeded draws keyed by (method, size, draw number), and the 57.4% door-pool share computed in model.js:59 so learner copy cannot drift from the sampler.

The correlation stratification: r = 0.81 across the year collapsing to 0.26/0.10/0.31 within seasons, with the association explicitly kept real ('it does not, by itself, tell you the direction or existence of a cause') and a line on what evidence would support a causal claim (app.js:332).

Honest free-text handling: the a3 self-review checklist with exemplar and the case-file review that checks structure, evidence words and over-claiming while saying plainly it does not judge whether the reasoning is right (index.html:223-231, app.js:380).
gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown University), the brief's own 10: its correlation chapter lets the learner drag individual points and watch r, the best-fit line and the residuals recompute live, so the learner perturbs the model itself rather than toggling layers over fixed data. Data Detective's activity 3 colours and stratifies 52 fixed weeks but never lets the learner move a point or see a different year; activity 2 never plots the % late-library quantity that carries the whole bias story, and no activity asks for a prediction before the model answers. The teaching is correct and complete; the interaction is one level short of the explainer the field points to.
